assertion: Drought covers almost 94% of the Lower Mississippi River system in mid-November, more than twice the drought extent in late July.
inaccuracy: 94% is D1-D4 for the three-state AR-LA-MS region (NIDIS Nov 12; warehouse Nov 10 94.7%, Nov 17 97.7%); the July base (42%) is dryness-or-drought (D0-D4) while 94% is D1-D4. Like-for-like D1-D4 rose from about 23% to 94%, so 'more than twice' understates.
independent_value: NIDIS Nov 12: 94% (94.2) of region in D1-D4

assertion: In late July, about 42% of the Lower Mississippi Valley region had dryness or drought in effect.
inaccuracy: Warehouse area-weighted D0-D4 for AR+LA+MS on Jul 28 is about 49%; the article's region or date may differ slightly.

assertion: That includes more than 90% of Arkansas, more than 80% of Mississippi, and more than 82% of Louisiana in Severe (D2), Extreme (D3), or Exceptional (D4) drought.
warehouse_value: D2-D4 Nov 17: AR 90.7%, MS 80.0%, LA 85.0% (area-weighted county estimate; MS at the margin)
independent_value: NIDIS Nov 12: 97% of AR in D1-D4

assertion: Arkansas is especially hard-hit, with almost 56% of the state in Exceptional Drought (D4).
All three states experienced their warmest August-October period on record, accompanied by near-record dryness (Third driest in Arkansas, fourth driest in Louisiana, and fifth driest in Mississippi).
warehouse_value: nClimDiv Aug-Oct 2026 mean temp rank 1 of 132 in AR (77.6F), LA (79.5F), MS (77.7F); driest rank AR 3, LA 4, MS 5
sql: RANK over Aug-Oct mean tmpc and summed pcpn, area_codes 003/016/022, 1895-2026

assertion: Arkansas, Louisiana and Mississippi all had less than 50% of normal precipitation in August. September brought less than 10% of normal amounts to Arkansas and northern Louisiana and less than 25% of normal amounts to northern Mississippi. And all three states had less than 10% of normal precipitation in October.
inaccuracy: Statewide nClimDiv vs 1991-2020 normals: August AR 50%, LA 51%, MS 60% (not under 50%); October AR 26%, LA 30%, MS 20% (not under 10%); September AR 35%. The article's figures plausibly describe sub-state hot spots, but are not true statewide as phrased. The NIDIS text's only '50%' is an unrelated D4 share.
why_not: The '50%' in the NIDIS page refers to Arkansas Exceptional Drought share, not precipitation, so it does not change the grade.

assertion: During the August-September-October period, temperatures in all but coastal sites were 5 to 9 degrees Fahrenheit above normal.
inaccuracy: Statewide Aug-Oct departures vs 1991-2020 are AR +6.2F, MS +4.1F, LA +3.5F (statewide averages include coastal areas); station-level 5-9F plausible, not directly verified.
measure: Mississippi Arkansas Louisiana August-October temperature departure
